channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: TSE desidrata portaria sobre planos de conformidade das plataformas digitais
item.description: TSE President Nunes Marques softened the initial draft of the digital platforms compliance plan regulation for the 2026 elections, partially accommodating company requests by extending deadlines for proposal submission (to August 16) and responses to electoral diligences (10 days, extendable by up to five). Core requirements remain, including the mandate for platforms with over 5 million monthly active users in Brazil to submit compliance plans, and the authority to impose direct regulatory supervision if plans are not delivered on time.

item.title: ‘Pix Pensão’: o que muda com nova lei que autoriza débito direto na conta
item.description: President Lula signed into law the 'Pix Pension' system, which mandates automatic debit payments for child support to reduce delinquency. Financial institutions must dedcourt-ordered amounts from the payer's account and notify authorities of insufficient funds, enabling asset seizure. He also approved a law requiring widespread publicity of the Ligue 180 hotline for women in high-traffic public spaces.

item.title: Caiado lidera no 2º turno contra Lula em GO, diz Genial/Quaest
item.description: Genial/Quaest poll shows Ronaldo Caiado leading in a hypothetical second-round presidential matchup against Lula in Goiás with 67% voter intention, compared to Lula’s 23%. In the first round, Caiado and Flávio Bolsonaro are technically tied at 33% and 27%, respectively. Lula is the most rejected candidate in Goiás, with 64% rejection among those familiar with him.

item.title: Deputados do PT levam à PF novas suspeitas sobre Flávio no Caso Master
item.description: PT deputies Lindbergh Farias and Rogério Correia filed a crime report with the Federal Police alleging that Flávio Bolsonaro pushed for an amendment to the General Environmental Licensing Law that reduced banks’ liability for environmental damage, benefiting Banco Master, which he is allegedly linked to. They claim he voted in favor of the bill in May 2025, proposed amendments in August, and voted to overturn the presidential veto in November 2025, ensuring the rule took effect. The accusation ties this to other investigations, including the 'Dark Horse' case and suspicious invoices involving Flávio and Daniel Vorcaro.

item.title: Moraes já envenenou a eleição
item.description: The text claims that Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes has already 'poisoned' the 2026 presidential election, suggesting his actions during the 2022 electoral process — particularly his role in investigations related to the January 8 attacks — are negatively shaping the current political climate. It argues that the Electoral Justice, under Moraes’ leadership, is fostering distrust and polarization, echoing the post-2022 election environment when Bolsonaro supporters rejected the result. The piece warns this dynamic could trigger renewed instability, including military barracks encampments and another attack on the Plaza of the Three Powers.

item.title: TSE abre a urna eletrônica para estudantes do Centro de Ensino Médio Elefante Branco, em Brasília
item.description: The TSE will open the UE2022 electronic ballot box for students at Centro de Ensino Médio Elefante Branco in Brasília on Monday (3) at 11h, as part of the National Week of the Electronic Voting System. The activity, led by Electoral Technology Coordinator Rafael Azevedo and substitute Minister Nauê Bernardo — both former students of the school — aims to educate youth on the security, transparency, and auditability of the Brazilian electoral system.

item.title: Os influenciadores de direita convocados por consulado dos EUA em SP para reuniões
item.description: The U.S. Consulate in São Paulo held meetings with right-wing influencers, including Maria Fernanda Schmidt, Leandro Narloch, Rafael Ferri, and Penélope Nova, all associated with the digital ecosystem supporting Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign. The Brazilian government and Planalto Palace interpreters view these gatherings as part of an international right-wing movement backing Bolsonaro’s candidacy. Participants emphasized the importance of freedom of expression in the digital space.

item.title: Lula diz que acionou Padilha para conseguir cirurgia a “companheiro”
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that he intervened with Health Minister Alexandre Padilha to secure the transfer of a 'companion' from Caraguatatuba (SP) awaiting heart surgery due to delays by the private health plan in verifying coverage. Speaking at the PSB national convention in Brasília, Lula criticized the bureaucracy of private health plans and defended the SUS as a system that must guarantee immediate treatment regardless of financial condition. He also linked tax deductions for private health plans to reduced government revenue that could otherwise serve the poor.

item.title: PT vai ao TSE contra Flávio Bolsonaro e diz que rival amplifica posts de IA com ataques a Lula
item.description: The PT filed a complaint with the TSE against Flávio Bolsonaro and four other politicians, accusing them of amplifying anonymous profiles that use AI to attack President Lula. The complaint alleges improper use of technology for electoral disinformation. The case was filed on July 30, 2026.

item.title: Presidente de Tribunal do DF pressiona por análise de contas de Ibaneis antes das eleições
item.description: The president of the Federal District's Court of Accounts, Manoel de Andrade, urged for an accelerated analysis of former Governor Ibaneis Rocha's (MDB) 2025 accounts before the October elections, despite delays in the BRB's financial statements. He argues the delay cannot justify postponing the judgment, which could determine Ibaneis' political future, as technical staff tend to recommend rejecting the accounts. However, rapporteur Paulo Tadeu insists on waiting for the BRB's balance sheet, deemed essential to assess the DF's patrimony, even though the district's accounts are formally separate from the bank.

item.title: Sem alianças, PL cogita vice do Novo para Flávio, mas aliados de Zema veem movimento como ‘troco’ após fala sobre Michelle
item.description: The PL is considering economist Marina Helena (Novo-SP) as a potential running mate for Flávio Bolsonaro due to difficulties in forming national alliances, but the move faces internal resistance within Bolsonaro's campaign and is seen by Novo as a 'retaliation' for Romeu Zema's comments about Michelle Bolsonaro. Marina Helena stated she has not received a formal invitation and remains focused on her federal deputy campaign. Despite her social media presence and appeal to liberal voters, Bolsonaro allies believe she would add little political or electoral value, given Novo's small congressional bloc.

item.title: O novo gesto de Michelle para acenar bandeira branca a Flávio às vésperas da campanha
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro removed from her Instagram two videos in which she accused Flávio Bolsonaro of mistreatment and disrespect, after publicly accepting his apology. The move comes ahead of her first public appearance with her stepson since the conflict, scheduled for Sunday, July 1st, at the PL convention in the Federal District, where she is expected to be launched as a Senate candidate. Allies aim to use the event to demonstrate family unity in Flávio’s presidential campaign.

item.title: Meio-Dia em Brasília: Lula quer tomar um cafezinho com Moraes
item.description: The Meio-Dia em Brasília program discussed Bolsonaro’s defense response to Minister Alexandre de Moraes regarding an AI-generated video of the former president, aired at the PL convention. It also covered President Lula’s expressed desire to have coffee with Moraes as a gesture of institutional rapprochement.

item.title: Como Lula e Flávio chegam aos maiores colégios eleitorais do Nordeste
item.description: Lula leads voter intention in the Northeast's three largest electoral colleges — Bahia, Pernambuco, and Ceará — with over 50% in the first round and advantages exceeding 30 points over Flávio Bolsonaro. In the second round, his lead remains strong, reaching up to 60% in Ceará. The Quaest surveys, conducted in July 2024, indicate a solid electoral base for the president in the region.

item.title: Aliado de Zema, Simões cita 'decepção' com Aro após anúncio de desembarque da chapa para candidatura própria
item.description: Minas Gerais Governor Mateus Simões (PSD) expressed disappointment after Marcelo Aro (PP), former state secretary and ally of Romeu Zema, announced he would run for governor in 2026, breaking from the governing coalition and aligning with the Republicanos party, linked to Eduardo Cunha. Simões said Aro had been sheltered in government for four years and that his candidacy depends on whether Senator Cleitinho changes his position.

item.title: A causa que une Sergio Moro e famosa criadora de conteúdo adulto
item.description: Adult content creator Larissa Ferrari met with Senator Sergio Moro and Deputy Rosangela Moro to discuss women's rights amid rising gender-based violence in Brazil. She emphasized her non-partisan commitment to protecting women and thanked them for their support. The meeting could be exploited by Moro's political rivals in his Paraná gubernatorial campaign, given his conservative base and potential backlash from evangelical voters over moral and family values.

item.title: PL insiste em Cleitinho, mas deixa decisão em MG para o Republicanos
item.description: The PL continues to prioritize Cleitinho Azevedo as its candidate for governor of Minas Gerais, despite the Republicans party blocking his run. The PL states the decision is an internal matter for Republicans and says it will not interfere, but reaffirms Cleitinho remains its top choice. If Cleitinho does not run, the PL is considering alternatives such as Marcelo Aro, whose prior support for Governor Matheus Simões could conflict with a gubernatorial bid.

item.title: Manual do Eleitor: sete mudanças nas regras de doações para as Eleições 2026
item.description: The TSE modernized donation rules for the 2026 elections, allowing Pix donations without electoral receipts and enabling digital opening of campaign accounts via electronic signatures. Despite simplification, donor identification and resource traceability remain mandatory, ensuring transparency. The resolution also expands inclusion for historically underrepresented groups and maintains the ban on cryptocurrency donations.

item.title: Interpol: saiba o que significa lista de difusão prateada que a PF avalia incluir Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The Federal Police is considering adding Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to Interpol's 'Silver Notice,' a 2025 pilot tool for international asset tracking aimed at locating and freezing property, bank accounts, and other assets linked to investigations. The move stems from an inquiry into the alleged misappropriation of R$ 61 million intended for the film 'Dark Horse,' which may have been transferred abroad via banker Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master.

item.title: Nova lei cria o “Pix Pensão”, para transferência automática de pensão alimentícia
item.description: President Lula signed Law 15.479/26, establishing 'Pix Pensão' for automatic child support payments via the Central Bank’s electronic system. The law allows beneficiaries to request automatic transfers at any stage of enforcement, with judges ordering direct debits from the payer’s account. It takes effect in one year and includes provisions for seizing funds from individual entrepreneurs’ accounts and publishing national statistics on child support cases.

item.title: Governo Lula decidiu que embaixador do Brasil retornará à Argentina
item.description: The Lula government has decided that Brazilian ambassador to Argentina Julio Bitelli will return to Buenos Aires, though not immediately. He was recalled for consultations following attacks by Argentine President Javier Milei against Lula at the National Convention of the Liberal Party (PL) in São Paulo.

item.title: Prestígio de Caiado impulsiona sucessor em Goiás, indica Quaest
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows 71% of Goiás voters believe former governor Ronaldo Caiado deserves to choose his successor, reflecting his enduring political influence in the state despite his national presidential ambitions. Caiado’s prestige is boosting the candidacy of his hand-picked successor for the 2026 Goiás gubernatorial race.

item.title: Zema cita Girão para vice, mas senador mantém foco no governo do Ceará
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo party's presidential candidate, cited Senator Eduardo Girão (Novo-CE) as the leading choice for vice president in a potential pure party ticket. However, Girão reaffirmed that his priority remains running for governor of Ceará, maintaining a state-level focus despite the national offer. The senator emphasized he is not negotiating the vice-presidential spot and remains committed to the Ceará campaign.

item.title: Caiado defende Petrobras estatal e expansão de refinarias
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, presidential candidate for the PSD, advocates keeping Petrobras as a state-owned company and expanding the country's refining capacity to reduce diesel imports and support agribusiness. He criticizes the current policy of reinjecting natural gas into oil wells, arguing it limits supply for fertilizer production, and opposes privatization, calling it 'foolish' and claiming only China would buy the company.

item.title: Argentina vai expulsar estrangeiros que promoverem ‘mensagens de ódio’ ao país
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei signed a decree modifying the Immigration Law to allow the expulsion of foreigners who promote hate speech against Argentina, its citizens, or national symbols, either orally or in writing. The measure follows international criticism and Milei’s claims of an alleged anti-Argentina campaign led by Brazil and other countries, linked to public clashes with Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and reactions to Argentina’s loss in the 2026 World Cup. The government states that political, ideological, or academic criticism remains protected under freedom of expression.

item.title: Assista e leia a íntegra do discurso de Tábata Amaral na convenção do PSB
item.description: Tábata Amaral (PSB-SP) spoke at the PSB national convention in Brasília, stating that the alliance between Geraldo Alckmin and Lula shows former adversaries can unite for democracy. She advocated for electing a Congress committed to national sovereignty, criticized lawmakers who 'turn their backs' on the people, and emphasized the PSB's goal of achieving 40% female representation in its federal caucus.

item.title: JOTA Principal: Moraes deve definir critérios para uso da imagem de Bolsonaro — não só por Flávio
item.description: Alexandre de Moraes, former president of the TSE, influences the 2026 elections by setting criteria for the use of Jair Bolsonaro's image in synthetic content, considering the former president's penal execution. His interpretation of deepfake, based on the TSE resolution, establishes barriers for candidates using Bolsonaro's image without authorization, with potential liability for non-compliance with judicial orders. This affects not only Flávio Bolsonaro but all candidates seeking to attract Bolsonaro's electorate.

item.title: Assista e leia a íntegra do discurso de João Campos na convenção do PSB
item.description: PSB national president João Campos spoke at the party's national convention in Brasília, formalizing Geraldo Alckmin as the vice-presidential candidate on the PT's ticket with Lula. He emphasized the alliance with President Lula as 'genuine' and 'true,' stating the PSB will support the duo in all 27 states and work for their re-election, while aiming to double its congressional caucus and increase female representation among elected federal deputies.

item.title: Diante de tensão com Milei, Lula convida Moraes para um café
item.description: President Lula invited Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes for coffee after signing the Pix Pension Alimony and Law 180 measures, a gesture made days after Argentine President Javier Milei criticized Moraes at a PL convention. Milei called Moraes 'bald trash,' prompting Lula to call Milei a 'thing,' escalating bilateral tensions that led Brazil to summon Argentina’s ambassador and recall its own envoy from Buenos Aires for consultations.

item.title: PF avalia incluir Flávio Bolsonaro em lista da Interpol para rastrear dinheiro do filme 'Dark Horse' no exterior
item.description: The Federal Police is considering including Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in Interpol's silver diffusion to trace alleged misappropriated funds from the financing of the film 'Dark Horse', linked to R$61 million transferred by former banker Daniel Vorcaro. The move follows the STF's authorization of an inquiry based on an audio in which Flávio demands the funds from Vorcaro, with suspicions that the money was sent abroad and diverted from its intended purpose.

item.title: Pesquisa: o duelo Lula x Flávio no estado que foi pivô da crise no clã Bolsonaro
item.description: In Ceará, Lula leads Flávio Bolsonaro 55% to 22% in the first round, with a 33-point advantage. In a potential runoff, Lula’s lead widens to 37 points (60% to 23%). The state is pivotal due to being the epicenter of a Bolsonarist crisis, marked by a rift between Flávio and Michelle Bolsonaro over local candidate support.

item.title: Cid Gomes e Capitão Wagner lideram corrida ao Senado do Ceará
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll released on July 30, 2026, shows Cid Gomes (PSB) and Capitão Wagner (União Brasil) leading the race for Ceará’s two Senate seats. Cid Gomes has a 36% rejection rate, while Capitão Wagner has 40%. In Scenario 3, Capitão Wagner and Eunício Oliveira (MDB) are technically tied. The survey interviewed 1,002 voters from July 24–28, with a 3-point margin of error and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Multa a Lula por discurso contrasta com tolerância a abusos do clã
item.description: The R$15,000 fine imposed on Lula by the TRE for prematurely mentioning votes contrasts with the tolerance shown by the STF and Minister Alexandre de Moraes toward Bolsonaro clan abuses, such as the use of an AI-generated video of Jair Bolsonaro at the PL convention, which violated TSE resolutions and house arrest restrictions. The defense attempts to shift blame to a 'butler,' but in fact exposes the liability of Flávio Bolsonaro and Valdemar Costa Neto, revealing a strategy to provoke judicial reactions to feed a narrative of political persecution.

item.title: Juliana Brizola e Zucco empatam na disputa pelo governo do RS
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll released on July 30, 2026 shows Juliana Brizola (PDT) and Luciano Zucco (PL) technically tied in the first round of the Rio Grande do Sul gubernatorial race, with 24% and 22% voting intentions, respectively. In a potential runoff, Brizola leads with 35% against Zucco’s 31%. The survey also found that 48% of voters approve of Governor Eduardo Leite’s (PSD) administration, while 42% disapprove.

item.title: PoderData/Aya: Lula é aprovado por 43% e desaprovado por 49%
item.description: Lula has a 43% approval and 49% disapproval rating in the PoderData/Aya poll from July 26–29, 2026, with 8% undecided. Approval dropped 3 points from the prior week (46% to 43%), while disapproval rose from 47% to 49%. On government performance, 44% approve and 50% disapprove, showing a 1-point increase in approval and a 1-point decrease in disapproval.

item.title: Sem voto obrigatório, 22% deixariam de ir às urnas
item.description: 22% of Brazilians would abstain from voting if voting were not mandatory, while 74% say they would still go to the polls even if it were voluntary. Among Lula supporters, 11% would abstain without compulsory voting, compared to 20% of Flávio’s voters, showing greater sensitivity to the change among his base. The survey, conducted by PoderData/Aya from July 26–29, 2026, with 2,400 interviews, has a 2-point margin of error and is registered with the TSE under BR-07845/2026.

item.title: Lula e Flávio têm 49% de rejeição cada um, diz PoderData/Aya
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro each have 49% rejection rates, according to a PoderData/Aya poll from July 2026. Both have solidified bases — 36% of voters say they would only vote for the petista and 31% only for the senator — making rejection reduction the key campaign challenge. For 16% of Brazilians, rejection of other candidates is the decisive factor in their vote choice.

item.title: PoderData/Aya: 62% escolhem candidato pela proposta que defendem
item.description: The PoderData/Aya poll shows that 62% of voters choose their candidate based on the proposals they defend, while 16% vote primarily out of rejection of other candidates. This group of voters motivated by exclusion is seen as crucial in the tight race between Lula and Flávio, as reducing one’s own rejection and winning over these voters could be vital to victory in October.

item.title: Lula tem 46% contra 43% de Flávio no 2º turno, diz PoderData/Aya
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are in a technical tie in a potential runoff with 46% and 43% respectively, within the 2-point margin of error. Lula leads the first round with 41%, followed by Flávio at 35%. The president maintains an advantage among women and in the North, Northeast and Southeast regions, while Flávio leads in the South and Central-West.

item.title: Transparência Internacional vê debate eleitoral sobre corrupção limitado a 'acusações' e lança recomendações a governadores
item.description: Transparency International-Brazil released 40 recommendations to combat corruption in state governments, criticizing electoral debates for limiting themselves to generic accusations. The NGO urges candidates to make concrete commitments on transparency, access to information, and anti-corruption mechanisms, based on the Public Transparency and Governance Index. The report aims to assist transition teams and new governments in setting priorities for the 2027–2030 mandates.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: em cenário de empate técnico no RS, Flávio Bolsonaro tem 32% e Lula, 30%, no 1º turno
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows a technical tie between Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) in Rio Grande do Sul, with 32% and 30% respectively in the first round. In a potential runoff, Bolsonaro leads with 40% against Lula's 35%.

item.title: Quaest no RS: Flávio tem 32%, e Lula, 30% das intenções de voto no estado
item.description: The Quaest poll in Rio Grande do Sul shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) with 32% and Lula (PT) with 30% in presidential voting intentions for 2026, technically tied within the margin of error. In runoff scenarios, Bolsonaro leads Lula 40% to 35%, while Lula leads Caiado (33% to 32%), Renan Santos (34% to 25%), and Zema (35% to 29%). The poll also reveals strong rejection of Lula’s government in the state, with 64% of voters saying he does not deserve a second term.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: com 55% no 1º turno, Lula lidera com folga corrida à Presidência no Ceará
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva leading presidential voting intentions in Ceará with 55%, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 22%. Other candidates each have less than 3%. Lula leads by a 33-point margin over the second-place candidate.

item.title: Repercussão de notas fiscais trouxe boa e má notícia para Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The issuance of invoices by Flávio Bolsonaro's law firm to companies linked to Banco Master triggered negative repercussions, with 37.8% of social media posts accusing corruption or money laundering. However, among those showing clear voting intent, 54.4% expressed support for the senator, indicating limited impact on his electoral base.

item.title: Com ou sem punição?
item.description: A survey of 490 readers found that 80.8% believe Jair Bolsonaro should be punished for using artificial intelligence to address participants at the PL convention that nominated his son Flávio as a presidential candidate. Only 13.9% opposed punishment, while 5.3% suggested he may not have known about the AI use. The result reflects widespread public concern over the ethical use of AI in political contexts.

item.title: Quando o Judiciário reescreve as regras do jogo
item.description: The TSE regulated AI use in 2024 electoral campaigns by requiring transparency but banning deep fakes intended to favor or harm candidacies. Holding Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign accountable for AI use raises concerns about rule predictability, given the tribunal already defined clear permitted limits. The controversy threatens the principle that electoral rules must be known in advance to ensure democratic legitimacy.

item.title: Quando os institutos de pesquisa disputam os mesmos eleitores
item.description: Brazil is experiencing a continuous flow of presidential election polls for 2026, with 69 national surveys conducted between January and June by 19 different institutes, creating an unprecedented environment of frequency and methodological diversity. This context differs from earlier studies based on face-to-face interviews, reflecting a technological transition and the formation of a new electoral polling ecosystem, although institute accuracy remains aligned with international standards.

item.title: Contador de Flávio preso no caso do INSS foi fiscalizado por conselho
item.description: The accountant from the law office of Flávio Bolsonaro, presidential candidate for PL-RJ, was arrested in the INSS embezzlement case and faced two professional council audits for irregularities in client declarations.

item.title: Raquel ganha apoios no PT e reforça voto 'Luquel' da esquerda em Pernambuco
item.description: Governor Raquel Lyra (PSD) secured informal endorsements from PT members and other left-wing forces in Pernambuco for her re-election bid, despite the party's official support for rival João Campos (PSB). These endorsements revived the 'Luquel' vote — a blend of Lula and Raquel — signaling an unusual alignment between some PT sympathizers and the governor's campaign.

item.title: Decisăo de Moraes sobre IA de Bolsonaro expőe embate com Nunes Marques
item.description: Alexandre de Moraes' decision regarding the AI-generated video of Jair Bolsonaro used in Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign launch highlights a clash between Moraes' stance and Kassio Nunes Marques' actions at the TSE. The case reveals tensions among justices over the use of technology in political campaigns and the Electoral Court's role in combating misinformation.
